required_interface.mesh: A finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded polyhedral open set; cells are nondegenerate, cover the closure, have disjoint interiors, and intersect face-to-face.
required_interface.broken_and_conforming_spaces: The broken space is the finite product of cellwise polynomial spaces; conformity requires equal traces on interior facets; zero boundary means zero polynomial trace on every boundary facet.
required_interface.sobolev_membership: For real-valued conforming polynomials on a finite matching mesh, the cellwise gradient is the weak gradient. With zero boundary facet trace and Countable Choice, the function lies in W^{1,p}_0 for finite p and satisfies the stated Poincare estimate.
required_interface.scope_used: Batch 57 uses only mesh, P0 broken-space, continuous P1 conformity, and zero-boundary interfaces. It makes no interpolation-rate or shape-regularity claim.

suppliers.source_excerpt:
def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes, Definition: “A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set of closed, nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$, their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a whole face of each.”

def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces, Definition: “The **broken polynomial space** is the finite product
$$V_h^{\mathrm{br}}:=\prod_{K\in\mathcal T}\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb K^q),$$
viewed as functions defined almost everywhere cell by cell.” The **conforming polynomial space** is
$$V_h^{\mathrm{conf}}:=\{v\in V_h^{\mathrm{br}}:v|_{F,K}=v|_{F,K'}\text{ on every interior facet }F\}.$$”

thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp, Statement: “Then $v\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$. Its weak gradient agrees almost everywhere on each cell with the ordinary cellwise polynomial gradient.”

thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p, Statement: “Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$”

required_interface.Galerkin_orthogonality: For a common variational equation and its conforming Galerkin solution, a(u-u_h,v_h)=0 for every v_h in V_h.
required_interface.Cea: For Countable Choice, a bounded coercive form on a Hilbert space, bounded conjugate-linear data, and finite-dimensional V_h, continuous and discrete solutions exist uniquely and satisfy the M/alpha estimate.

suppliers.source_excerpt:
lem-galerkin-orthogonality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations, Statement: “If $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ satisfy
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V),\qquad a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h),$$
then
$$a(u-u_h,v_h)=0\qquad\text{for every }v_h\in V_h.$$”

thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations, Statement: “The solutions satisfy
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac M\alpha\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$”

cor-symmetric-galerkin-best-approximation-in-energy-norm, Statement: “and suppose additionally that $a$ is Hermitian:
$a(v,w)=\overline{a(w,v)}$. Then
$$\|v\|_a:=\sqrt{a(v,v)}$$
is the energy norm and the Galerkin solution is its best approximation:
$$\|u-u_h\|_a=\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_a.$$”
